newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe's sick queue for life in strike-hit city.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe's sick queue for life in strike-hit city.

text.p: Long queues of sick people are waiting for hours in the hot sun at clinics and surgeries in Zimbabwe's capital Harare where major hospitals have closed down due to a devastating strike by nurses and doctors.
At a clinic in the capital's Mbare township, one queue snaked for about 500 metres (yards) on Thursday.

"The only guarantee that you will get some treatment is if you are brought in an ambulance," said Masauso Phiri, who said he was suffering from chronic diarrhoea and had been running in and out of the clinic's toilet "all day".
Others in the queue, most of whom looked listless, ignored reporters' questions.
A nurse at the clinic -- working with her back against a fading poster promising "Health for All by the Year 2000" -- refused to talk to reporters.
"We are not allowed...and you are not allowed here unless you are seeking treatment," she said sharply.

Authorities at the southern African state's two largest hospitals -- Harare and Parirenyatwa -- discharged the sick into the hands of relatives and friends on Wednesday after almost all medical staff walked out in protest at the arrest of two doctors accused of inciting nurses to strike.

Zimbabwean riot police sealed off on Thursday a city park after rumours swept Harare that angry relatives of the sick planned to march there. Striking nurses have often used the park as a rallying point. Police officials refused to comment.
Many Zimbabweans say their relatives have died unnecessarily in the past two weeks due to lack of treatment and blame the government for failing to resolve the crisis.
A mortuary attendant at Harare Hospital, where some people were weeping inconsolably, said many people were dying at home.
"We are seeing a lot of BIDs (brought in dead) since the strike began and yet the deaths from hospitals has remained the same while fewer people are being admitted," he said.
